what_it_does: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) lets a computer perform calculations directly on encrypted data without ever decrypting it — useful for private AI inference where the data should never be exposed. The cost is that each encrypted multiplication consumes a resource called a multiplicative level, and when those levels run out, a very expensive reset operation called bootstrapping is needed to restore capacity. Minimizing the number of bootstrappings is therefore critical to performance. ReSBM is a compiler optimization that formulates finding the best bootstrapping insertion points as a graph-cutting problem — it models the computation as a network of nodes and finds the smallest set of cuts (the min-cut) that prevents any path from running out of levels. This guarantees a provably minimal number of bootstrapping operations, reducing overhead in encrypted machine learning inference.
